quote: I had here you were the homeowner. Was it you and your wife?
stewart_read: Rep proactively surfaces co-ownership during verify, which is good practice, but never follows up later to explicitly confirm the wife will be present at the in-person Friday visit. Because this is an in-person appointment rather than a phone appointment, her absence is unconfirmed rather than a confirmed exclusion — a softer gap than a phone-appointment spouse exclusion.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be relying on the in-person format itself to naturally include whoever is home, making explicit spouse confirmation less critical than on a phone appointment.
coaching_implication: When co-ownership is confirmed early, the rep should close the loop near button-up: 'Will your wife be able to be there Friday morning too?' Costs one sentence and removes ambiguity for the closer.

quote: I know you you might not know, but do you have any idea of, like, an average price you guys are normally paying every month? No idea, bro.
stewart_read: Bill amount was not captured — customer has no idea what he pays. Rep acknowledges and moves on without attempting any alternative anchor (e.g., asking about kWh usage habits, AC use, home size) that could still create bill-pain framing.
alternative_hypothesis: Since the customer flagged early that his wife handles all bills, the rep may have reasonably judged that pressing for a number here was low-yield and better deferred to the bill-photo request later in the call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to still plant a value hook even without a number: something like 'no worries, once we get the bill photo we'll know exactly what you're paying and can show the savings' — ties the unknown number to a concrete next step instead of just dropping it.

quote: Yeah. It might not be for a little while. She just opened her own, retail business, but she's over there right now.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a scheduling/logistics anchor (wife busy at her new business) that the rep could reflect back to set a soft deadline or check-in point; instead the rep simply accepts the delay and moves to confirming the phone number for texting.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally not pressuring the customer given the clear time constraints already disclosed (two businesses, four kids), prioritizing goodwill over urgency.
coaching_implication: A light touch like 'no rush, whenever she gets a free minute at the shop' would have cost nothing and reinforced warmth while still keeping the ask alive.

quote: We I have two businesses. She has one, all retail. We have four kids. They're all in sports. I coach football, baseball, basketball. It's like, we just never literally get a free minute in it.
stewart_read: Customer opens up significantly about his life and businesses; the rep engages warmly in the moment (asking about the businesses) but the extended rapport exchange is not bridged back into any qualification value — it stays purely social.
alternative_hypothesis: The rapport itself may be the value here — building trust with a talkative customer who volunteers his own scheduling constraints, which the rep then successfully uses to lock a Friday morning slot.
coaching_implication: Not a hard miss, but the manager should note this is time spent on pure rapport with no qualification payoff (no bill, no second verify item surfaced) — fine occasionally, worth tracking if it becomes a pattern for this rep.

quote: How long does something like that take? Do you know? Just a quote? Somebody just kinda walking around and
stewart_read: Customer asks a legitimate logistics question (appointment length) which the rep answers directly and appropriately — this is not scope creep since it's a scheduling question, not product/pricing content.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here; flagging only to show the rep correctly distinguished a logistics question from a closer-tier question.

quote: Yeah. So let's do the first two in person Friday morning.
stewart_read: Rep locks day, channel, and eventually time, but the call ends without the full button-up sequence — no explicit one-hour block statement, no 'is that fair?' handshake, and no stated text-confirmation promise beyond the bill-photo text already discussed.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did partially button up by confirming day, time, and channel, and the customer independently confirmed ('I'll put you down for tennis, Friday'), so the appointment isn't fully unanchored — but the formal handshake elements are missing.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close with the standard button-up line set even on warm, cooperative calls: state the hour block, confirm no-driving/computer-or-in-person logistics, and get an explicit 'does that work for you?' rather than letting the customer's own summary substitute for it.
